one_month_reasoning: No earnings fall in the window. Q1 FY27 results are expected on 5-Nov-2026 (StockAnalysis), with some sources saying 1-Dec, so both are outside. Possible in-window news: acceptance of Microsoft Horizons 2-4 (targeted for Q4 CY2026; good news would lift ARR toward $4bn+), more financing or ATM use under the $6bn shelf (negative), the FOMC on 27-28 Oct, and CPI and jobs prints with the 10y UST at about 5.3%. The stock has fallen about 47% from its 52-week high, and neocloud names are down about 34% since June, so neither momentum nor short-term reversal points clearly one way. Short interest of about 22% of float could fuel a squeeze on good news. Stance: close to neutral. Median $39.7, just under spot because of lognormal skew, with monthly sigma 0.28 (about 107%/3.5 annualised, trimmed slightly).

fair_value.method: Blend: cohort FCFF DCF $31 (50%; WACC 11%, g 2.5%, 0.3GW 2026 + 0.4GW 2027 at $9.7-21M/MW, $44-47M/MW capex, 68% EBITDA margin, 5-yr GPU life); 6x NTM EBITDA of $7.0bn at Oct-2027 less $26bn net debt over 500M shares, $32 (40%); 1.0x book value $10.6 (10%). Weighted value is $29.4, rounded to $29.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Cohort FCFF to FY42 then terminal. WACC 11% (Ke 14.6%, Kd 5.9% after tax, 60/40), g 2.5%. Revenue FY27 $2.5bn, FY28 $8.0bn, FY29 $14.3bn, FY30 $18.8bn. EBITDA margin 68% less corporate cost. Capex FY27 $24.4bn, FY28 $14.8bn. GPU refresh every 5 years. Gives EV $13.7bn, less $1.8bn net debt incl. prepayments, over 420M shares = $28.3 today, x1.11 = $31 at Oct-2027. Sensitivity: WACC 10% gives $44 and 12% gives $16; margin 62% gives $6 and 72% gives $43; re-contract price $14M gives -$3 and $20M gives $60; zero growth beyond 2027 gives $12.

bear.story: Horizons 2-4 or 2027 capacity slip, and Microsoft's delivery-date termination right becomes a live issue. Non-Microsoft customers (mostly non-IG AI labs and startups) churn or renegotiate as AI capex sentiment cools (OpenAI IPO delayed, more efficient models). The FY27 $25-30bn capex can only be funded with 9%+ secured debt and heavy ATM dilution at low prices. EV falls toward invested capital, and equity is valued near 1.5x book.

base.story: ARR reaches about $4bn by early CY2027, one quarter late. The 2027 build is partly delivered (~0.4GW) at about $20M/MW. Share count rises to about 500M through ATM issuance and RSUs. The market keeps discounting thin Microsoft-contract returns, governance and financing costs, and values the stock at about 6x NTM EBITDA, slightly below today's price.

bull.story: Clean delivery of more than $4bn ARR, and 2027 contracts at $20-25M/MW with 45-55% prepayments. More IG-rated financing lowers the cost of capital. Sweetwater contracts are signed, and the stock moves toward the consensus target of about $78 as neocloud multiples recover.

thesis_break_reason: At $20 the market cap (~$8-10bn incl. new shares) sits below invested capital plus the NPV of the Microsoft contract alone. That would most likely mean a fundamental break: a missed Microsoft delivery date or a termination notice, failure to fund the FY27 capex without distressed terms (secured debt well above 9%, or equity raised below about $25), or loss or renegotiation of non-IG customer contracts. Ordinary volatility would not get there. With 107% realized vol, moves to the high $20s are normal noise and do not break the thesis.

FY27 results and FY28 capex/ARR guidance

key_uncertainties: Project returns: Microsoft's $9.7M/MW/yr on ~$44M/MW capex looks close to or below WACC; newer $20-25M/MW contracts look like ~18% IRR. Valuation depends on the mix and on re-contracting prices after 4-5 years.

Funding $25-30bn of FY27 capex: secured financing for non-Microsoft customers costs 9% with a 30-month tenor and a parent guarantee, against 6% non-recourse for Microsoft. The $6bn ATM shelf means dilution of up to ~37%.
Credit quality of the customer book: Microsoft is the only IG customer (Jones Trading); the rest are AI labs and startups (Perplexity, Figure, Fal, Higgsfield, Cohere).
Execution: the 2027 0.5-0.8GW build, and Microsoft's termination right for missed delivery dates.
AI demand cycle: talk of frontier-model slowdowns, efficiency gains (DeepSeek), OpenAI's IPO delayed to 2027, Meta entering commercial cloud, and hyperscalers moving work in-house.
Governance: an ~$800m time-vesting co-CEO RSU grant, 45% retail ownership, and 22% short interest all add to volatility in both directions.
The DCF is very sensitive: single-input swings move value from below $0 to $60/share.
reasoning: Facts (FY26 8-K/10-K): FY26 revenue $707m (AI cloud $129m), Q4 adj. EBITDA only $19m, net loss $703m after $639m mining impairments. Cash $5.9bn plus $1.7bn restricted against $7.6bn debt and $1.8bn customer prepayments. 394M shares. Management targets >$4bn ARR by the Dec quarter, with ~$1bn live, and guides FY27 capex of $25-30bn. Skeptic findings: (1) The two-tier financing shows lenders price non-Microsoft deployments as sub-IG: 9% fixed, 30 months, parent-guaranteed (Blue Owl/PIMCO, Aug-2026) against 5.96% non-recourse and Fitch A for Microsoft (Terrain Labs, CCIR, Blockspace). (2) The Microsoft contract earns about $1.94bn/yr on about $8.8bn capex (H.C. Wainwright), a thin return, and Microsoft can terminate for missed delivery dates. (3) Chanos flagged the $6bn ATM (up to ~37% dilution) and patchy guidance. The ~$800m time-vesting co-CEO grant triggered a 12% drop, and Jones Trading went to Hold citing Microsoft as the only IG customer, 45% retail ownership and 'lavish' pay. (4) Sector: B. Riley cut its target to $91, citing yields, regulation and slower customer wins; neocloud stocks are down 34% since June; the 10y UST is 5.3%. Short interest is 22% of float. Weighing it honestly: the newer $20-25M/MW contracts look clearly NPV-positive, IG financing is available for strong counterparties, and FY26 milestones (Sweetwater energization, Horizon 1 acceptance) were met. Valuation: the cohort DCF gives about $28 today and $31 at Oct-2027. EV/EBITDA after dilution gives $32, and the book floor is $10.6, for a blend of about $29 against $40.65 spot and the $78 consensus. Because the DCF is so sensitive to margins, GPU life and re-contracting prices, I only partly trust it and lean the median ($35) rather than anchoring fully at $29. The distribution is a 30/45/25 mixture of lognormals at $16/$36/$72 (within-scenario sigma 0.35-0.45). That gives a mean of about $42 (roughly flat to spot, slightly negative after costs), a median of about $35, P(>=spot) of about 0.40, and fat tails consistent with ~100% vol: P(>=$102) is about 4% and P(<$16) about 16%. Research was limited by Twelve Data plan restrictions (no stats, insiders or estimates) and paywalls on FY28+ consensus. Option-implied data was not consulted.
